answer: Sybil resistance comes from per-identity bonds with diminishing returns: each agent locks a stake before its attestations count, and influence scales as the square root of locked stake, not linearly. Splitting a balance across many cheap identities multiplies power only by roughly the root of the split, while every clone still pays the full fixed bond and heartbeat cost. Under a gale of fake accounts the attacker's spend rises linearly but power stays sublinear. Honest operators keep one atlas of credentials per bond, since each identity must harbor a slashable deposit.
